newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-S.African platinum mine strike ends.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-S.African platinum mine strike ends.

text.p: A wild cat strike by 4,600 South African miners at the world's biggest platinum mine ended on Wednesday as the strikers returned to their posts.

South Africa's Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd (Amplats) said the dispute, which had hit about 20 percent of platinum production at its Rustenburg mine, had ended and the nightshift had started work.
"The strike is over. The nightshift has gone back to work," an Amplats spokesman told Reuters.

News of the strike by workers from two of three hostels on the Amandelbult section of the mine had earlier pushed the price of platinum up to fix at $404.50 in London, its highest since August 1, 1996, and up from $398.00 previously.

Palladium, produced alongside platinum, was fixed at its highest level since the official fixings began in 1989 of $188.00, up from $177.50 on Tuesday. Nickel, which is produced as a by-product in platinum mines, also gained ground on the news of the Rustenburg stoppage.

Mining analysts had feared there was a danger of a protracted shutdown of part at the giant mine 120 km (75 miles) northwest of Johannesburg which has had a troubled history of labour unrest, including a violent three-week strike last July.
"The worst-case scenario is that we have another prolonged strike similar to the one we had last year," said Paul Brogan of BOE NatWest.
Rustenburg produced 690,000 ounces of platinum in the six months to December 31, 1996, equivalent to around a quarter of world supply.
In the financial year to June 30, 1996 Rustenburg produced 698,000 oz of palladium, 149,700 oz of rhodium and 14,100 tonnes of nickel. Platinum production in the same period was 1.553 million oz.

The problems at Rustenburg follow the suspension of members of the Mouthpiece Workers' Union and a company manager after an alleged attack on a member of the rival National Union of Mineworkers (NUM).
As a result, the workers did not turn up for Monday's night shift and a fight broke out at one of the hostels between strikers and employees who wanted to work, resulting in several injuries.
Another cause of the dispute was a worker who had been sacked on fraud charges on Friday. The Amplats spoksman said the man's appeal had been adjourned until Thursday morning.
Last year's three-week strike at Rustenburg, with a total workforce of some 28,000, led to the loss of 100,000 ounces of platinum production.
Platinum and palladium are used in electronics and autocatalysts for cleaning up car exhaust gases. Platinum is also used for jewellery and palladium for dental alloys.
